Multinomial Regression with Grouped or CLR Entrywise L0 Penalties

L0glm_multinomial.Rd

Joint multinomial IRLS with centered log-ratio (CLR) coefficients, an invariant grouped L0 penalty, and an optional entrywise CLR L0 penalty.

Details

For \(C\) categories, use family=mgcv::multinom(K=C-1). Supply a factor/class vector or an integer count matrix with \(C\) columns. Every category must have positive weighted training count. For count vectors, \(N_i=\sum_cY_{ic}\) and $$p_{ic}=\exp(\eta_{ic})/\sum_h\exp(\eta_{ih}),\qquad \eta_i=x_i^TB+o_i,\qquad B\mathbf{1}=0.$$ Thus \(\eta_{ic}=\log p_{ic}-C^{-1}\sum_h\log p_{ih}\) for centered offsets. The weighted likelihood includes the multinomial count constants. A factor is a one-trial count response.

All \(C\) coefficient columns are returned in CLR coordinates, in original predictor units. An unrestricted, unpenalized intercept is added by default. predict(type="link") returns centered scores; predict(type="response") returns probabilities; and predict(type="class") returns class labels. Starting matrices, prior means and offsets have \(C\) columns in response category order and are centered across categories. A starting row supplied as all zero excludes that predictor before CLR centering, throughout selection and relaxed refitting. Individual category zeroes within other starting rows remain eligible. Intercepts and always.include rows remain eligible even with zero starts. Scalar start=1 centers to zero but keeps all rows eligible; start=0 fits only mandatory terms. A weak-ridge step seeds eligible zero starts before adaptive weighting. The returned sparse coefficient matrix retains all original predictor rows and \(C\) category columns, with excluded rows filled with zeroes. Use start=NULL for automatic initialization. nonnegative=TRUE is ignored with a warning.

prior.mean supplies ridge-penalty targets in original predictor units. Supply a \(p\) by \(C\) matrix in response-category order, including any added intercept row. Targets are transformed internally and centered to CLR: $$a_{jc}\leftarrow a_{jc}-C^{-1}\sum_{h=1}^C a_{jh}.$$ Common row shifts have no effect. A scalar or length-\(p\) vector is repeated across categories and therefore gives zero CLR targets; nonzero targets require category contrasts. NULL uses zero targets. The quadratic ridge term is centered on these targets, whereas adaptive weights and support counts still use coefficients relative to zero. Targets are not starting coefficients and do not override starting-row exclusions: a nonzero target for an excluded row leaves that row fixed at zero in the full-size sparse output. Unpenalized intercept/mandatory rows are not shrunk toward their targets. The final relaxed refit removes the ridge penalty on retained support, so the targets no longer exert shrinkage during that refit.

Joint quadratic IRLS

The observation score and information on class scores are $$s_i=w_i(Y_i-N_ip_i),\qquad W_i=w_iN_i\{\operatorname{diag}(p_i)-p_ip_i^T\}.$$ The class covariance has null direction \(\mathbf{1}\). An orthonormal basis \(Q\) with \(Q^TQ=I\) and \(Q^T\mathbf{1}=0\) eliminates that redundant direction in the linear solve. Writing \(B=\Gamma Q^T\) preserves \(\|B_j\|_2=\|\Gamma_j\|_2\). The exact class covariance, including off-diagonal class coupling, is used. These are weighted least-squares IRLS steps, algebraically equivalent to Newton/Fisher scoring for multinomial logit. Independent marginal binomial fits, or centering their coefficients, do not solve this likelihood.

Tall working systems assemble coefficient-space curvature. Wide systems whiten observation/class blocks and use the existing Woodbury ridge path. Dense or stacked working arrays can arise even for sparse predictors. control.family$max.working=2000L guards the smaller working dimension. The optional control.family=list(multinomial="bound") replaces exact curvature by the upper bound \(0.5I\) on the contrast plane, while retaining the exact likelihood and constraints. The bound is inspired by Krishnapuram et al.; their sparse penalty is L1, not the adaptive L0 procedure here.

Selection, invariance and degrees of freedom

With grouped=TRUE, the target is $$-2\ell(B)+\lambda\sum_{j\notin M} \mathbf{1}\{\|B_j\|_2>0\},$$ where \(M\) contains mandatory terms. In normalized working CLR coefficients \(b\), adaptive ridge diagonals are \(D_{jc}=\lambda/(4\|b_j\|_2^2)\). The exponent is fixed at two, with \(\|b_j\|_2^2=\sum_h b_{jh}^2\). Positive and negative class effects cannot cancel in this norm. Both the row penalty and the model are invariant to the choice of orthonormal contrast basis and to permutations of category labels.

With grouped=FALSE, the charge counts nonzero displayed CLR entries, and \(D_{jc}=\lambda/(4|b_{jc}|^2)\). This is a different sparsity target from entrywise ILR sparsity. Each active row is solved on the zero-sum plane of its allowed class entries; a row with fewer than two entries must be zero. Adaptive weights are unsmoothed and use coefficients relative to zero, not deviations from prior.mean; thresh does not alter them. With grouped=TRUE, hard thresholding acts on \(r_j=\|b_j\|_2\), not individual category entries or arithmetic row means. An entire row is removed if \(r_j<\texttt{thresh}\max_{k\in S}r_k\) or \(r_j<10^{-20}\), where \(S\) contains selectable, nonmandatory rows. Very small category entries in a retained row are not individually hard thresholded. With grouped=FALSE, each category column instead uses \(|b_{jc}|<\texttt{thresh}\max_{k\in S}|b_{kc}|\) or \(|b_{jc}|<10^{-20}\). Surviving entries are then recentered within their allowed set to preserve zero-sum rows, while removed entries remain zero; rows with fewer than two allowed entries are zero. Mandatory rows are exempt and excluded from cutoff maxima. Thresholded entries or rows remain excluded during selection. Cutoffs use normalized working coordinates; selectable slopes equal original-unit coefficients times the stored column scales. normalize="none" gives scale one. The default cutoff is thresh=1e-5. Setting thresh=0 removes only the relative cutoff. These cutoffs apply only during selection with lambda>0.

With relaxed=TRUE, a final joint multinomial IRLS pass uses lambda=0 and disables hard thresholding. A grouped refit admits all category entries in retained predictor rows, so previously zero category entries within those rows can become nonzero. An ungrouped refit admits only the selected nonzero CLR entries and fixes other category entries at zero. Both preserve zero-sum rows: \(s\) admitted entries give \(s-1\) free directions, and a nonzero row needs at least two nonzero entries. No new predictor rows can enter. Explicit all-zero starting rows remain excluded; intercept and always.include rows remain eligible and unpenalized. Sparse output retains all original predictor rows and category columns. Grouping defaults to TRUE, and relaxed fitting defaults to TRUE for grouped multinomial models with either factor or count-matrix responses. Set relaxed=TRUE explicitly to refit an ungrouped model. Each selection or relaxed pass has its own maxit limit; group.maxit is unused.

metrics$objective uses the requested L0 charge. GIC_rows charges selected rows. Parameter-count ICs instead use \(C-1\) free directions per grouped row, or \(s_j-1\) for a row with \(s_j\) active CLR entries, plus mandatory directions. Grouped IC tuning uses the row criterion. The algorithm is a subset-selection heuristic and does not certify global optimality. These loops are serial. Check convergence, especially under separation or at small regularization values.

References

Krishnapuram, B., Carin, L., Figueiredo, M. A. T. and Hartemink, A. J. (2005). Sparse multinomial logistic regression: Fast algorithms and generalization bounds. IEEE TPAMI 27(6), 957–968.

See also

L0glm.fit, L0glm.tune, L0glm.metrics, multinom

Examples

if (requireNamespace("mgcv", quietly = TRUE)) {
  set.seed(202)
  X <- matrix(rnorm(300 * 6), 300, 6)
  eta <- cbind(0, 0.2 + X[, 1] - 0.6 * X[, 2],
               -0.3 - 0.8 * X[, 1] + 0.7 * X[, 3])
  P <- exp(eta - apply(eta, 1, max))
  P <- P / rowSums(P)
  y <- factor(vapply(seq_len(nrow(X)), function(i)
    sample.int(3, 1, prob = P[i, ]), integer(1)))
  fit_multinomial <- L0glm.fit(X, y, family = mgcv::multinom(K = 2),
    lambda = "gic", grouped = TRUE, relaxed = TRUE,
    maxit = 200, tol = 1e-8)
  fit_multinomial$coefficients
  fit_multinomial$convergence
  max(abs(Matrix::rowSums(fit_multinomial$coefficients)))
  head(predict(fit_multinomial))
  L0glm.metrics(fit_multinomial)
}
